newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates stay low amid good supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates stay low amid good supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates remained at lower levels on Friday amid abundant supply of kuna funds although demand ahead of end-of-week payments rose, dealers said.
"There was a large amount of both call money and term funds on offer," one dealer said, putting the total supply at more than 125 million kuna against demand for 47.5 million.
"Demand has grown... It is Friday and all banks count with bigger payouts," the dealer said.
To meet higher needs, the banking sector was welcoming the central bank payment of some 450 million kuna today for its Wednesday's purchase of hard currency.
It had eight million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, unchanged from Thursday night, a central bank official said.
The morning money market demand was met in full. Term loans amounted to more than a half of fresh deals struck by 0900 GMT.
One-month borrowings were made at 11 percent, unchanged from Thursday, when the rate was cut from 13 percent.
One two-month loan was granted at 13 percent and a three-week loan at 9.0 percent.
Call money was steady at 7.0 percent.

Thursday's overnight trade totalled 17.5 million kuna, of which six million went to three banks with shortfalls. The rest was granted to two banks and one savings bank for maintenance of their mandatory reserves.
